SL-000026.transcript:
Member (Tyler Fortin): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Tyler Fortin, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Fortin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Fortin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Fortin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): How old is he?
Member (Tyler Fortin): Fourteen.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Tyler Fortin): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Tyler Fortin): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Tyler Fortin): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Tyler Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Tyler Fortin): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Tyler Fortin): Great, that helps.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Tyler Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
SL-000026.narrative_summary: Tyler Fortin, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a coverage question case. Agent Ryan MacDonald checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 4 (satisfied).

Member (Emma Morrison): I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Emma Morrison, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Morrison): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Morrison): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Morrison): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which policy is this about?
Member (Emma Morrison): My term life policy. It renewed this month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did you get a confirmation of the cancellation?
Member (Emma Morrison): No, I was told it would be processed.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?
Member (Emma Morrison): Yes, same account.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): If the cost came down, would you want to keep some coverage?
Member (Emma Morrison): Maybe, if it's affordable.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the policy billing history and the forms received.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I can see your call from the 17th and the renewal payment taken on the 1st.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The renewal rate is higher because the policy moved into a new age band on renewal.
Member (Emma Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The cancellation was processed after the renewal draft had already gone through. I've requested the refund, and it'll be back in your account within seven business days.
Member (Emma Morrison): So I get the full 750 back?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes, the full amount. The refund request is approved and goes back to the same account.
Member (Emma Morrison): Will I get something in writing?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Yes, a cancellation confirmation by mail within ten days.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Emma Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-000073.transcript:
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Mathieu Ahmed, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Which plan is the transfer from?
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): My old employer's pension plan. I left the company in May.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Where is the money going?
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Have you received any statement showing the transfer as pending?
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): Only the annual statement, which still shows the balance with you.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): Who follows up?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Mathieu Ahmed): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
SL-000073.narrative_summary: Mathieu Ahmed, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a group retirement transfer case. Agent Sophie Belanger traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account. In the end, it was resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 2 (dissatisfied).

Member (Tyler Kim): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Tyler Kim, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Kim): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Kim): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Tyler Kim): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Tyler Kim): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Tyler Kim): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Tyler Kim): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Tyler Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Tyler Kim): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Tyler Kim): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Tyler Kim): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Tyler Kim): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Mathieu O'Brien, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?

Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Mathieu O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Lavoie): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Emma Lavoie, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Lavoie): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Emma Lavoie): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): How old is he?
Member (Emma Lavoie): Fourteen.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Emma Lavoie): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.

Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Emma Lavoie): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Great, that helps.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Emma Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Singh): I cancelled my life insurance before it renewed and you still took the payment.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Liam Singh, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Singh): It went from about 250 to 750 dollars a month.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Singh): I called two weeks before the renewal date to cancel.

Member (Liam Singh): No, I was told it would be processed.

Member (Liam Singh): 750 dollars on the 1st.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is the payment still coming from the same bank account?

Member (Liam Singh): How much would a lower amount cost?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Halving the coverage brings it to about 375 dollars a month. The comparison I'm sending shows a few options.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: the new rate follows the renewal schedule, I've sent you the notice and a lower-coverage option, and you can decide within 30 days.
Member (Liam Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Member (Leila Ahmed): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Leila Ahmed, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Ahmed): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): Which procedure was the request for?

Member (Leila Ahmed): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Leila Ahmed): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Leila Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Tyler Lavoie): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Tyler Lavoie, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Yes, that's right.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): How old is he?
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Fourteen.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Tyler Lavoie): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Yes, here in town.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Great, that helps.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Tyler Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Noah Cote): The pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Noah Cote, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Cote): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Cote): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Noah Cote): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which medication or service is the request about?
Member (Noah Cote): A new medication my specialist started me on last week.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Noah Cote): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which pharmacy are you using?

Member (Noah Cote): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Noah Cote): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Noah Cote): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Lucas Martin): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Lucas Martin, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Lucas Martin): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Lucas Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Lucas Martin): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Lucas Martin): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Lucas Martin): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Lucas Martin): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Lucas Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Owen Morrison): I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Owen Morrison, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Morrison): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Morrison): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Owen Morrison): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you know roughly when HR sent their statement?
Member (Owen Morrison): They said about three weeks ago, but I haven't seen anything confirming it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Owen Morrison): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Owen Morrison): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Owen Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Owen Morrison): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Owen Morrison): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Owen Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Leila Kim): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Leila Kim, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Leila Kim): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Good question to ask before you commit. Let me look.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Leila Kim): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Leila Kim): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): How old is he?
Member (Leila Kim): Fourteen.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Is the orthodontist here in Canada?
Member (Leila Kim): Yes, here in town.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Leila Kim): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Leila Kim): Great, that helps.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Leila Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.

Member (Arjun Lavoie): Who follows up?

Member (Chantal Campbell): I want to check whether my plan covers orthodontics for my son.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Chantal Campbell, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Campbell): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Chantal Campbell): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Chantal Campbell): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Chantal Campbell): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Chantal Campbell): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Chantal Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Chantal Campbell): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Chantal Campbell): Great, that helps.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Chantal Campbell): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Emma Campbell): I'm following up again — the pharmacy said my new prescription needs another form before you'll cover it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Emma Campbell, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Emma Campbell): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Emma Campbell): I uploaded the prescription through the app already.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Emma Campbell): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Emma Campbell): My doctor charges 45 dollars to fill in forms.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Did the pharmacy give you the name of the form they need?
Member (Emma Campbell): They said 'prior authorization' and gave me a number to call. That's it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Which pharmacy are you using?
Member (Emma Campbell): The one near my work. They said they can resubmit as soon as it's approved.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is your doctor's office aware a form is needed?

Agent (Priya Sandhu): For this medication the plan needs a prior authorization from your doctor, not just the prescription.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm checking whether anything from your doctor's office is already on file.
Member (Emma Campbell): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The drug is on the prior authorization list, so we need the completed form from your doctor before it can be covered. I've emailed you the form and noted that you're waiting on it.
Member (Emma Campbell): And I'm paying the doctor for the form on top of everything.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. Keep the receipt for the form, and I'll note on your file how much medication you have left.
Member (Emma Campbell): How long does the review take once it's in?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Usually two to three business days. I've asked for it to be prioritised given your supply.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the form is in your email, your doctor completes and faxes it, and the review usually takes two to three business days.
Member (Emma Campbell): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.

Member (Mei Fortin): I'm following up again — I've been off work for six weeks and still haven't had a decision on my short-term disability claim.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Mei Fortin, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Fortin): I already explained this on my last contact.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I'm sorry about that — let me look at what happened last time and pick up from there.
Member (Mei Fortin): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Mei Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Mei Fortin): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Mei Fortin): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Mei Fortin): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Mei Fortin): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Mei Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Mei Fortin): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Mei Fortin): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Mei Fortin): That's not really the answer I was hoping for, but okay.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I've logged everything here so if this comes up again, the next agent has the full picture.
